Writing clean code is a skill that every programmer should develop. The main goal is to make your code readable, not just for the computer, but for other humans who will work with it later. One of the first steps is to follow naming conventions. Instead of using vague names like `x` or `data`, choose descriptive ones such as `userTotal` or `isLoggedIn`. This makes the purpose of each variable obvious at a glance.

Another important practice is to break your code into small, focused functions. Each function should do one thing well, rather than handling many tasks at once. This not only simplifies testing but also improves maintainability. When you need to fix a bug or add a feature, you can quickly find the right place to make changes. In the end, clean code saves time, reduces errors, and makes collaboration much easier.
